sources.bowDrag: Her logs' sawn ends meet the water face on: a flat-faced cylinder in axial flow has a drag coefficient of 0.8 to 1.1, a flat disc 1.17 (Hoerner 1965, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 3)
sources.sideDrag: Across her she is a wide, shallow section with rounded corners, side ratio 3 to 5 once mirrored at the surface: 1.0 to 1.3 sharp-edged (Delany & Sorensen 1953, NACA TN 3038), less with round logs, lowered again by her finite length (Hoerner 1965, ch. 3)
sources.sweepMetres: Her rower's seat is 0.69 m aft of her middle and the blade swept at arm's length works some 0.7 m beyond her 0.67 m half-beam, 0.69 aft and 1.37 m out: 1.53 m from her middle
sources.pole: Poled standing on her logs toward the side he poles, 0.14 m above the water: a raft of logs bears a man standing far more stiffly than any canoe (bin/lib/hulls/physics.py), and a log raft is poled standing (Territory Stories, Northern Territory Library). His hands end the shove at his hip, 0.93 m over his soles (0.530 of a 1.756 m stature: Drillis & Contini 1966; ANSUR II, Gordon et al. 2014); his eyes at vanilla's standing 1.7 m
